title: Burst smoothing and priority fairness hotpatch to restore tokens/sec stability for mixed-model workloads
creator: Sofia Patel
description:
Summary: After the 2026-03-09 scheduler change to dynamic burst windows, we observed sustained tokens/sec degradation and TTFT spikes for customers running mixed short-chat + long-completion workloads. The root cause appears to be priority inversion during burst smoothing: long requests hold batching windows open and starve small, latency-sensitive requests. This ticket coordinates a targeted hotpatch to enforce fairness and immediate mitigation for Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments.

Observed behavior: - 2-3x TTFT increase for small requests during regional bursts - 30-50% drop in tokens/sec across mid-tier Dedicated clusters - Customer escalations: two enterprise customers reported app-level timeouts and a production incident (Pager duty) - Affected models: gpt-medium family and several open LLM adapters when multiplexed

Goals: - Implement burst-smoothing policy that enforces per-priority token quotas in active batch windows - Add a fast-path bypass for sub-20-token requests during congestion - Deploy a staged hotfix (canary -> region roll) across Hosted, Dedicated, Private (VPC) - Restore stable tokens/sec and bring TTFT back within SLOs
reproduction_steps: 1) Send mixed workload: 60% long (>=512 tokens) open-ended completions, 40% short chitchat (<=20 tokens) to the same model pool.
2) Observe batching diagnostics (batch_size, wait_time) from runtime traces for 10 minutes.
3) Compare TTFT and tokens/sec pre/post scheduler change using rtx-dashboard link in attachments.
investigations: 01 2026-03-09 18:40 - Alerts detected: region-us-central tokens/sec drop; triggered incident.
02 2026-03-10 08:00 - Reproduced locally with stress harness using mixed request generator (link in attachments).
03 2026-03-11 14:20 - Heap/profile traces showed long requests occupying KV cache slots and batch headroom.
04 2026-03-12 11:10 - Kernel selector logs show multiplexed workers waiting on smaller requests; priority inversion confirmed.
decisions: A: Implement per-priority token cap per batch window (immediate hotpatch).
B: Add bypass fast-path for short requests (<20 tokens) to avoid batch queuing under high load.
C: Rollout plan: canary on hosted-us-east, then dedicated clusters, then private customers with opt-in toggles.
actions_taken: Canary deployed to hosted-us-east (2026-03-12 20:30) with monitoring enabled.
current_status_notes: Canary results (12h): TTFT for short requests improved by 42% in canary region; tokens/sec normalized to within 8% of baseline. One Dedicated customer saw partial improvement; Private deployments require manual patching guidance.
Follow-up: edge-case where long requests still absorb KV cache; added ticket to evict stale KV entries for long-running sessions (ENG-158789).
next_steps: 1) Merge PR after two approvals and run full CI (target merge: 2026-03-13 12:00).
2) Apply hotfix to Dedicated staging and small Private pilot (2026-03-13 afternoon).
3) Monitor 72-hour metrics and collect customer feedback; prepare rollback plan if regressions detected.
4) Postmortem and permanent solution roadmap (adaptive batching + KV eviction) in runtime-stability project.
